data.narrative:
EX-Fusion is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Kazuki Matsuo, Shinsuke Fujioka, and Yoshitaka Mori, with $37M in total capital raised. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 comparable companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Valar Atomics, Helion, Oklo, and X-Energy, all operating in the same sector at similar or adjacent development stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $37M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, implies a valuation of $74M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics (Series B, $6.0B), Nano Nuclear Energy (Seed, $808M), and Fuse Energy (Series A, $200M)—yields a median of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer range reflects substantial stage and technology-maturity variation within the nuclear energy sector.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $63M to $929M, with a median of $441M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around technology execution risk and market timing in early-stage fusion development. Stage-progression alone suggests the low end; peer comparables anchor toward the middle and upper range. Key uncertainties include engineering feasibility validation and regulatory pathway clarity.
